notes.note: Ambiguous iteration order: tested the reading given by the example sequence ([0][0], [0][1], [1][0], [1][1], last index varies fastest). Replies are queued at [1][0] and [0][1]; [0][1] must be selected.

Syntactically a variable reference in the signature template is indistinguishable from a matching value; the test passes unassigned variables for the out/inout parameters as if they were assignment targets. Titan accepts it (no such check; it would fail at runtime on the unbound variables).
Runtime condition ('at the time of the operation'), so verdict is ttcn3verdict:error. Titan does not raise an error for a null from clause (the branch simply does not match; observed verdict fail).
'Completely initialized port array' is not defined further; the test uses 'any from' on a single port (not a port array), following the ETSI conformance test NegSem_220304_getreply_operation_001.
Without a from clause the actual sender type is only known at runtime, so verdict is ttcn3verdict:error (cf. NOTE 3). Titan performs no runtime check (observed verdict fail).
Informative NOTE; tests the statically detectable case (return value of type integer redirected into a charstring variable).

Titan accepts the incompatible decmatch (Int) / @decoded target (charstring) combination; Titan does not implement restriction k. The encode attribute on Int is only needed so that decmatch is legal; no decoding is executed.
Tested as a reject test: exception list contains two structurally identical record types, and the raise omits the type field.
Connections are created dynamically, so the missing to clause in a one-to-many connection is detected at runtime: ttcn3verdict:error.
